projects.title: Galactic Arms Race
projects.summary: A multiplayer Diablo-esque looter shooter whose weapons are evolved by neural networks while you play. Also the thesis game for cgNEAT (content generation with AI).
bullets: CPPNs (compositional pattern-producing networks) generate the weapon patterns.
Fitness rises with each shot fired from a weapon and falls when another weapon is used, so the gene pool evolves toward what players actually like.
The gene pool is drawn from every weapon on the current server.
GOFAI for player drone interactions.
32-player online multiplayer using Lidgren networking.
Steam integration: achievements via Steamworks and cloud save/load.
awards: Best AI in an Independent Game (Editor's Choice)

projects.title: Agentic AI workflows
projects.summary: A human asks a coding agent for a change. The coding agent then commands sub-agents inside the running game to exercise it, verify the results, and do their own testing. I also built workflows that let non-coders ship changes.

projects.title: JanssEngine
projects.summary: My own engine and renderer, built from the ground up: dual OpenGL/DirectX renderer, Lua integration, my own JanScript language, LOD terrain, BSP with PVS, and hot-reloadable DLL plugins.
bullets: Dual renderer interface: swap between OpenGL and DirectX.
Lua integration with native code access, plus JanScript, my own scripting language.
LOD terrain from binary terrain files; BSP with collision, frustum culling, and potentially visible sets.
Collada loading and a custom 3ds Max exporter (Dj3d) with animation and skinning.
DLL plugin loader with live reload, threaded background loading, hierarchical clocks and profiling.
Data-driven, classless game object loader using XML and named properties.
Memory manager, string pool, intrusive smart pointers, fixed-point math, and a computational geometry library.

projects.title: NEAT auto-balancer
projects.summary: Neuroevolution that balances a game. It takes every unit's health and attack damage as input and outputs attack cooldowns that hit a desired lock/unlock chart. Agents earn fitness per balanced unit and category (max 32), and the run stops when one balances the whole game.

projects.title: AI Battle — 2nd place
projects.summary: A battle for food and survival between programmed AIs. My cockroach-like agents build and share a light map and try to move toward darkness. Walls, enemies, and dirt emit light, and found food emits darkness toward the nearest unit. Took 2nd place overall.

projects.title: Braaains!
projects.summary: A top-down 2D zombie shooter whose zombies use neuroevolution to adapt to how you play in real time. Sensors for the player and bullets go in, and rotation, velocity, dodges, and lunges come out.

projects.title: Robot Vision
projects.summary: An edge and line detection pipeline: Sobel for gradient magnitude and direction, then Canny for peaks and valleys, then Burns for the N longest lines within an angle threshold.

projects.title: Editors & pipelines

about: I'm a game programmer who loves the parts players feel: tight controls, juicy feedback, rock-solid multiplayer, and frame times that never hitch. I've led Skyrim VR from conception to launch, led Starfield's StarMap, and today I own Voidwood's deterministic rollback simulation at Santa Barbara Games.

Lately I've been building agentic AI workflows where coding agents drive in-game sub-agents to test and verify their own work. To me, reading code and understanding exactly what it does at a low level now matters more than typing it.
Off the clock I'm a competitive gamer (8th of ~80,000 in GameStop's Super Smash Bros. Brawl national grand finals; Evolve Top 100 Goliath), a game jam regular, and happiest on a river in a canoe.
